- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Malintzin's life before the Spanish conquest of Mexico is limited in detail, primarily derived from Spanish accounts written post-conquest.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Malintzin was born into a noble family in the Gulf Coast region of Mexico and was taken captive by the Aztecs as a young woman.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Malintzin was given to Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés as a gift and interpreter, fluent in both Nahuatl and Mayan.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Malintzin was believed to be highly intelligent and resourceful, using her knowledge to serve as an advisor and mediator between the Spanish and Aztecs.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] She helped the Spanish navigate Aztec society, build alliances with indigenous leaders, and communicate with a wider range of indigenous peoples than Jerónimo de Aguilar.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Little is known about Malintzin's life before the conquest, and many aspects of her story are debated among historians.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Malintzin's role in the Spanish conquest of Mexico and her legacy as a symbol of the intersections of Aztec and Spanish cultures are significant in Mexican history.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Malintzin's marriage was part of a broader pattern of intermarriage between Spanish men and indigenous women during the colonial period.
